annotations.title: Post my event to my TikTok

description: Posts the host's event to the host's OWN TikTok account: the event's photo card, the same post the Sonar Connections dashboard's Post to TikTok panel makes, through the same server door. Only a host or organizer of the event can post, and only to the TikTok account they connected themselves. `eventId` names the event. `mode` is post (published now) or draft (sent to the host's TikTok inbox to finish there). For a post, `privacyLevel` is REQUIRED and has no default: it is one of the options TikTok offers this account; call without it and the reply lists them (`privacyLevelOptions`), then ask the host who can view the post and call again with their pick. While Sonar Connections is in TikTok's review, TikTok accepts private posts only (SELF_ONLY, only the host can view); say so if the host asks for a wider audience. `caption` is optional (up to 4000 characters, no links, times or street address); without it the event name is the caption. `allowComments` is off unless the host asks for comments. `disclose` is off unless the host says the post promotes their own brand (`yourBrand`) or is paid or branded content (`brandedContent`); branded content cannot be private. Repeat the host's choices back and get a clear yes first: the call posts. Not connected: the reply carries a one-tap connect link (`url`) with a `message`; give both exactly and tell them not to forward it. The reply's `state` is posted, saved, processing or failed, with a `line` to read out; refusals (NOT_SIGNED_IN, not_enabled, forbidden, privacy_mismatch, branded_private, bad_title) are read out as given. It requires a personal connector token.

allowComments.description: Optional: true only when the host wants comments. Default false.

caption.description: Optional: the caption, in the host's words.

disclose.description: Optional: {yourBrand, brandedContent}, each true only when the host says so. Default off.

mode.description: post publishes now; draft sends it to the host's TikTok inbox to finish there.

privacyLevel.description: Who can view a post: one of the privacyLevelOptions TikTok offers this account. Required for a post; the host picks it.
